headline: Record revenue, but margin and profit compress on mix
summary_short: Trex posted record Q2 net sales of $418.0M, up 7.8% y/y on broad-based volume growth, but gross margin fell to 37.9% from 40.8% and net income dropped 18.5% y/y to $61.9M ($0.60 diluted EPS) on mix shift, Arkansas depreciation, and a $5M non-cash equipment write-down.
summary_long: Revenue growth was volume-driven and broad-based across products, price points, and channels, with pricing a minor contributor. Gross margin compressed 290bps y/y on a higher mix of railing sales, increased Arkansas depreciation, and temporary production inefficiencies from uneven in-quarter demand. SG&A rose 21.1% y/y (16.1% of sales) on branding/marketing investment. Net income fell to $61.9M, also pressured by a $5M non-cash write-down of obsolete equipment. Free cash flow was $181.8M; the company repurchased ~$51M of stock and repaid $130M of revolver borrowings, with a further $150M buyback approved. Management reaffirmed FY2026 guidance (net sales $1.215-1.250B, adjusted EBITDA $335-350M) and issued Q3 net sales guidance of $305-320M, while accelerating the Arkansas ramp to Q3 2026.

drivers.explanation: Revenue accelerated on broad-based volume strength and an upgraded distribution network, but a railing-heavy mix, Arkansas depreciation, production inefficiencies, and a one-time write-down pulled margins and net income down y/y.
Growth was volume-driven and broad-based across product categories, price points, and distribution channels, with pricing contributing minimally.
Impacted by a higher mix of railing sales, increased Arkansas-facility depreciation, and temporary production inefficiencies from uneven in-quarter demand patterns.
Increase reflects investments in capabilities and continued branding/marketing spend to accelerate consumer demand and support future growth.
Margin compression and higher SG&A were compounded by a $5 million non-cash write-down of obsolete equipment, recorded in other expenses.
Decline mirrors the GAAP operating-income pressure from mix and cost inflation, only partly offset by adding back the equipment write-down and higher depreciation.
Release does not explain the y/y decline directly; it attributes the quarter's $181.8M level to a seasonal working-capital benefit and lower capex as Arkansas nears completion.
Share count fell as the company repurchased ~$153.6M of stock over H1 2026 (including ~$51M in Q2), with a further $150M buyback approved for H2.
Decline is fully explained by treasury stock rising to $1,063.8M from $912.3M on buybacks, outpacing the retained-earnings gain from net income.
